pr_summary: Implement a new boolean parameter `singleprecision` on the high-level `apply_transforms` function in ANTsPy. When True, the underlying transformation should be performed in single precision (float32), but the function must still return an ANTsImage whose pixeltype matches the supplied moving image. The returned image must preserve the physical space of the fixed image.
special_system_dependencies: ANTs core C++ library (built from source via scripts/configure_ANTsPy.sh)
patch_file_cues: The fix modifies the apply_transforms function to support float32 computation
test_file_cues: tests/test_core_ants_transform.py - whitespace fixes in test patch
Tests verify pixeltype preservation, physical space consistency, and sum similarity
platform_constraint_evidence: Shell scripts (configure_ITK.sh, configure_ANTsPy.sh) are bash scripts for Linux/Unix
setup.py uses platform.system() checks but supports Linux, macOS, and Windows
No Windows-only or macOS-only restrictions for the fix/test path
The touched file (ants/registration/apply_transforms.py) is pure Python, cross-platform
notes: ANTsPy is a Python wrapper around the C++ ANTs medical image processing library. The project requires building ITK and ANTs C++ libraries from source during installation. The test suite uses unittest framework. The fix adds a singleprecision parameter to apply_transforms() function. The repository supports Linux, macOS, and Windows, but CI testing primarily targets Linux (ubuntu-20.04). The project uses conda for CI environment management but can be installed via pip.
